Promotional Movie Ticket Offer Surfaces for 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran' Amid Court-Ordered Release Delay

A promotional campaign offering free tickets for the upcoming dark romantic thriller *Tu Hai Meri Kiran*, starring Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal, has appeared online via third-party deal platforms. However, the film's theatrical release currently remains on hold following a Bombay High Court order.

Understanding the Ticket Promotion

According to details shared by promotional deal trackers, the offer is hosted on an external page (tu-hai-meri-kiran.rewardzpromo.com) attributed to CineRewardz. Participants are prompted to submit personal details—including a full name, mobile number, and email address—followed by selecting a preferred city, participating theatre, date, and showtime. If processed successfully, tickets are reportedly dispatched via email and SMS.

Independent observers emphasize that promotional offers of this nature carry inherent uncertainties. The hosting page does not explicitly state a definitive expiration date, ticket quantity limits, or clear terms regarding availability, meaning ticket allocation cannot be guaranteed.

Release Status and Legal Context

*Tu Hai Meri Kiran*, featuring the tagline “She found a connection, he found an obsession,” was initially scheduled to hit theatres on October 23, 2026. However, a Bombay High Court order issued on October 19, 2026, placed the release on hold due to an ongoing financial dispute valued at Rs 8.85 crore. Because of this legal pause, official screenings may not be actively running or listed on mainstream ticketing platforms like BookMyShow.

Practical Implications and Reader Safety

For consumers evaluating online promotional offers, security experts and consumer advocates recommend adhering to strict safety guidelines:

  • Never Pay Fees: Legitimate promotional giveaways do not require payment. Users should never pay money, booking fees, or processing charges to claim free tickets.
  • Protect Sensitive Data: Do not share One-Time Passwords (OTPs), UPI PINs, banking passwords, or full credit/debit card details on promotional entry forms.
  • Consider Privacy: Entering contact information into third-party promotional pages may result in marketing communications. Users should use caution regarding what data they submit.

What is Confirmed Versus Unknown

  • Confirmed: A third-party promotional page is collecting user details for *Tu Hai Meri Kiran* ticket requests, and the Bombay High Court ordered a hold on the film's October 23, 2026 release date following a financial dispute.
  • Unknown: It remains unverified whether submitted requests guarantee free tickets, how long the promotion will remain active, and when the legal hold on the film will be resolved to allow a new theatrical release date.

Readers can verify showtimes and official theatrical availability directly through established ticketing platforms like BookMyShow and review the promotional context directly via the Original Source Announcement.
